rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the Prophet frowned because Ibn Umm Maktum pressed past the guide who had been signaled to restrain him, insisting on speaking; this involved some roughness from him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد: إنما عبس النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لابن أم مكتوم وأعرض عنه لأنه أشار إلى الذي كان يقوده أن يكفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an first reports the rebuke in the third person to honor the Prophet, then turns to direct address to reassure him.
rows.anchor: ثم أقبل عليه بمواجهة الخطاب تأنيسا له فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the primary reading, “he” is Ibn Umm Maktum, who may be purified by the Qur'an and religious instruction, gaining purity and losing ignorance.
rows.anchor: { لعله } يعني ابن أم مكتوم { يزكى } بما استدعى منك تعليمه إياه من القرآن والدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “he” refers to the unbeliever: the Prophet hoped he might accept Islam, but could not know whether that hope would come true.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الضمير في «لعله» للكافر يعني إنك إذا طمعت في أن يتزكى بالإسلام أو يذكر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan lengthens the initial hamza as an interrogative; “an” then depends on an omitted verb implied by “he frowned and turned away,” and this reading pauses after “turned away.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن «آأن جاءه الأعمى» بالمد على الاستفهام ف «أن» متعلقة بفعل محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common declarative reading does not pause after “turned away,” unlike al-Hasan's interrogative reading.
rows.anchor: فيوقف على هذه القراءة على «وتولى»، ولا يوقف عليه على قراءة الخبر، وهي قراءة العامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He compares this rebuke with the commands not to expel or avert one's eyes from worshippers in al-An'am and al-Kahf.
rows.anchor: نظير هذه الآية في العتاب قوله تعالى في سورة الأنعام: ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Or be admonished” means take heed of what you say; “the reminder may benefit him” means the admonition itself.
rows.anchor: { أو يذكر } يتعظ بما تقول { فتنفعه الذكرى } أي العظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading has “fatanafaʿuhu” in the indicative, coordinated with “yazzakka.”
rows.anchor: وقراءة العامة «فتنفعه» بضم العين، عطفا على «يزكى»

rows.speaker: عاصم وابن أبي إسحاق وعيسى
rows.claim: Asim, Ibn Abi Ishaq, and Isa read the verb in the subjunctive as a response to “laʿalla,” which is non-assertive; the reading is also attributed to al-Sulami and Zirr ibn Hubaysh.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وابن أبي إسحاق وعيسى «فتنفعه» نصبا. وهي قراءة السلمي وزر بن حبيش، على جواب لعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Whoever considers himself independent” is a person with wealth and riches.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { أما من استغنى } أي كان ذا ثروة وغنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taṣaddā means to turn toward someone and listen attentively to what he says.
rows.anchor: { فأنت له تصدى } أي تعرض له، وتصغي لكلامه. والتصدي: الإصغاء قال الراعي

rows.speaker: الراعي
rows.claim: Al-Ra'i's verse illustrates taṣaddā as leaning or attending toward a person.
rows.anchor: قال الراعي: تصدى لوضاح كأن جبينه سراج الدجى يحني إليه الأساور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One etymology derives taṣaddā from ṣadd, what faces or stands opposite; “my house is ṣadad his house” means directly opposite it.
rows.anchor: وأصله تتصدد من الصد، وهو ما استقبلك، وصار قبالتك يقال: داري صدد داره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another derivation relates it to ṣadā, thirst: the Prophet approaches the man as a thirsty person approaches water; muṣādāh can also mean opposition.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من الصدى وهو العطش. أي تتعرض له كما يتعرض العطشان للماء، والمصاداة: المعارضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading has the light form, dropping the second tā for ease of pronunciation.
rows.anchor: وقراءة العامة «تصدى» بالتخفيف، على طرح التاء الثانية تخفيفا

rows.speaker: نافع وابن محيصن
rows.claim: Nafi and Ibn Muhaysin read the form with gemination through assimilation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن محيض بالتشديد على الإدغام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbeliever's failure to be guided or believe is not the Prophet's responsibility; he is responsible only for conveying the message.
rows.anchor: أي لا يهتدي هذا الكافر ولا يؤمن، إنما أنت رسول، ما عليك إلا البلاغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person who comes eagerly is seeking knowledge for God's sake.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { وأما من جآءك يسعى } يطلب العلم لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “While he fears” means that he fears God.
rows.anchor: { وهو يخشى } أي يخاف الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet turns his face away from this seeker and occupies himself with someone else; talahhā derives from tat lahhā, to be distracted from something, and can mean deliberate inattention.
rows.anchor: { فأنت عنه تلهى } أي تعرض عنه بوجهك وتشغل بغيره. وأصله تتلهى يقال: لهيت عن الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forms lahītu ʿanhu and talaytu ʿanhu have the same meaning.
rows.anchor: والتلهي: التغافل. ولهيت عنه وتليت: بمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Safīr means a messenger or a peacemaker between people, with plural sufaraʾ; in Hebrew usage, paper makers or copyists are also called sufaraʾ.
rows.anchor: والسفير: الرسول والمصلح بين القوم، والجمع: سفراء، مثل فقيه وفقهاء. ويقال للوراقين سفراء، بلغة العبرانية

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the safarah are Qur'an readers because they read books; he also transmits the view attributed to Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: السفرة هنا: هم القراء، لأنهم يقرؤون الأسفار. وعنه أيضا كقول ابن عباس

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih identifies the safarah as the Companions of the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب بن منبه: «بأيدي سفرة. كرام بررة» هم أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi accepts that the Companions were noble and righteous but rejects them as the referent here: safarah, unqualified, is a designation specific to angels.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي: لقد كان أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سفرة، كراما بررة، ولكن ليسوا بمرادفين بهذه الآية

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports the Prophet's comparison: a proficient memorizer of the Qur'an is with the noble, righteous scribes, while one who recites with difficulty and keeps at it receives two rewards; the report is agreed upon, with Bukhari's wording.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi explains “noble” as noble in the sight of their Lord.
rows.anchor: { كرام } أي كرام على ربهم قاله الكلبي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan explains “noble” as keeping themselves above sins.
rows.anchor: الحسن: كرام عن المعاصي، فهم يرفعون أنفسهم عنها

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak transmits from Ibn Abbas that the angels are too noble to accompany a person when alone with his spouse or relieving himself.
rows.anchor: وروى الضحاك عن ابن عباس في «كرام» قال: يتكرمون أن يكونوا مع ابن آدم إذا خلا بزوجته، أو تبرز لغائطه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the angels prefer other people's benefits to their own.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أي يؤثرون منافع غيرهم على منافع أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Barrarah is the plural of bārr, following patterns such as kāfir/kafarah, sāhir/saharah, and fājir/fajarah.
rows.anchor: { بررة } جمع بار مثل كافر وكفرة، وساحر وسحرة، وفاجر وفجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Barr and bārr describe one fit for truth; birr in an oath is truthfulness, and the angels are obedient to God and sincere and truthful in their deeds.
rows.anchor: يقال: بر وبار إذا كان أهلا للصدق، ومنه بر فلان في يمينه: أي صدق، وفلان يبر خالقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He connects the noble, righteous angels with the description of the protected Qur'an and the purified who touch it in al-Waqi'ah.
rows.anchor: وقد مضى في سورة «الواقعة» قوله تعالى: إنه لقرآن كريم * في كتاب مكنون * لا يمسه إلا المطهرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qutila here can mean “cursed”; another explanation is “punished.” The human meant is the unbeliever.
rows.anchor: «قتل» أي لعن. وقيل: عذب. والإنسان الكافر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says that whenever the Qur'an says “the human was killed/cursed,” it means the unbeliever.
rows.anchor: روى الأعمش عن مجاهد قال: ما كان في القرآن «قتل الإنسان» فإنما عني به الكافر

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak reports from Ibn Abbas that the verse was revealed about Utbah ibn Abi Lahab, who had believed but renounced the Qur'an after al-Najm, accepting all of it except that surah; the Prophet prayed for a lion to be set on him, and a lion killed him at al-Ghadirah on a Syrian journey despite his companions' precautions. His father had said Muhammad had never spoken falsely.
rows.anchor: وروى الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال: نزلت في عتبة بن أبي لهب، وكان قد آمن، فلما نزلت «والنجم» ارتد

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Abu Salih transmits Ibn Abbas's gloss as an exclamation: “How much has he disbelieved!”
rows.anchor: وروى أبو صالح عن ابن عباس «ما أكفره»: أي شيء أكفره؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On one account “mā” is exclamative, like Arab curses used to express astonishment; the command is to marvel at the human's disbelief in the blessings described next.
rows.anchor: وقيل: «ما» تعجب وعادة العرب إذا تعجبوا من شيء قالوا: قاتله الله ما أحسنه!

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another exclamative reading marvels at how much the human disbelieves in God and His blessings despite knowing His abundant kindness.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ما أكفره بالله ونعمه مع معرفته بكثرة إحسانه إليه على التعجب أيضا

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj glosses the exclamation as “How severe his disbelief is!”
rows.anchor: قال ابن جريح أي ما أشد كفره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, mā is interrogative: what could have driven him to disbelief? The question rebukes him; mā can be exclamative or interrogative (meaning ayy).
rows.anchor: وقيل: «ما» استفهام أي أي شيء دعاه إلى الكفر فهو استفهام توبيخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks what God created this unbeliever from that he should act arrogantly, and calls people to marvel at his creation.
rows.anchor: أي من أي شيء خلق الله هذا الكافر فيتكبر؟ أي اعجبوا لخلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He was created from a small, base, lifeless quantity of fluid; why, then, is he deceived about himself?
rows.anchor: { من نطفة } أي من ماء يسير مهين جماد { خلقه } فلم يغلط في نفسه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan asks how one can be arrogant when one came out twice from the passage of urine.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: كيف يتكبر من خرج من سبيل البول مرتين

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak reports from Ibn Abbas that God determined the fetus's hands, feet, eyes and other parts, beauty or ugliness, height, and whether it would be wretched or fortunate.
rows.anchor: كذا روى الضحاك عن ابن عباس: أي قدر يديه ورجليه وعينيه وسائر آرابه، وحسنا ودميما، وقصيرا وطويلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss takes qaddarahu to mean proportioned him, as in the parallels cited from al-Kahf and al-Infitar.
rows.anchor: وقيل: «فقدره» أي فسواه كما قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God determined the human in stages, from a drop to a clot until his creation was complete.
rows.anchor: وقيل: «فقدره» أطوارا أي من حال إلى حال نطفة ثم علقة، إلى أن تم خلقه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء وقتادة والسدي ومقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, in a report through Ata, along with Qatada, al-Suddi, and Muqatil, says God made the path out of the mother's womb easy.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء وقتادة والسدي ومقاتل: يسره للخروج من بطن أمه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says God made the paths of good and evil clear, supported by the guidance and two paths mentioned elsewhere; Hasan, Ata, and Ibn Abbas through Abu Salih also give this view.
rows.anchor: مجاهد: يسره لطريق الخير والشر أي بين له ذلك. دليله: إنا هديناه السبيل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid also glosses the path as the path of wretchedness and felicity.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد أيضا قال: سبيل الشقاء والسعادة

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets the path as Islam.
rows.anchor: ابن زيد: سبيل الإسلام

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Tahir says God makes easy for each person what He created and decreed for that person, supported by the Prophet's saying that everyone is facilitated toward what he was created for.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو بكر بن طاهر: يسر على كل أحد ما خلقه له، وقدره عليه دليله قوله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says: act, for each person is facilitated toward what he was created for.
rows.anchor: وقدره عليه دليله قوله عليه السلام:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is directed to those who deny resurrection.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { يأيها الإنسان } خاطب بهذا منكري البعث

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the human addressed as al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الإنسان هنا: الوليد بن المغيرة

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima identifies the human as Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: أبي بن خلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed about Abu al-Ashadd ibn Kalda al-Jumahi.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في أبي الأشد بن كلدة الجمحي. عن ابن عباس أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question means: what led you to disbelieve in your Lord, the Generous, who overlooks your sins?
rows.anchor: « ما غرك بربك الكريم » أي ما الذي غرك حتى كفرت؟ «بربك الكريم» أي المتجاوز عنك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the devil assigned to the person deceived him.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: غره شيطانه المسلط عليه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says his wicked devil deceived him.
rows.anchor: الحسن: غره شيطانه الخبيث

rows.speaker: الحسن عن عمر
rows.claim: A report from al-Hasan, from Umar, says that foolishness and ignorance deceived him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: حمقه وجهله. رواه الحسن عن عمر رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Ghalib al-Hanafi reports that when the Prophet recited the verse, he said that ignorance had deceived the person.
rows.anchor: لما قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Salih ibn Mismar says it reached them that the Prophet recited the verse and said ignorance had deceived the person.
rows.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar links the explanation to God's description of the human as unjust and ignorant.
rows.anchor: وقال عمر رضي الله عنه: كما قال الله تعالى إنه كان ظلوما جهولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God's forbearance deceived the sinner because He did not punish him the first time.
rows.anchor: وقيل: غره عفو الله، إذ لم يعاقبه في أول مرة

rows.speaker: الفضيل بن عياض
rows.claim: Asked what he would answer if God asked him this on Judgment Day, al-Fudayl ibn Iyad says God's lowered veils of concealment deceived him, since generous can mean one who conceals.
rows.anchor: قيل للفضيل ابن عياض: لو أقامك الله تعالى يوم القيامة بين يديه

rows.speaker: ابن السماك
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sammak's poem warns the sinner that God's reprieve and long concealment are what deceived him.
rows.anchor: نظمه ابن السماك فقال: يا كاتم الذنب أما تستحي والله في الخلوة ثانيكا غرك من ربك إمهاله

rows.speaker: ذو النون المصري
rows.claim: Dhu al-Nun al-Misri says many people are deceived while living under concealment without realizing it.
rows.anchor: وقال ذو النون المصري: كم من مغرور تحت الستر وهو لا يشعر

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر الأبهري
rows.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Tahir al-Abhari's poem addresses the arrogant: God granted respite, but the person confronted Him with sins without fearing their consequence.
rows.anchor: وأنشد أبو بكر بن طاهر الأبهري: يا من غلا في العجب والتيه وغره طول تماديه أملى لك الله فبارزته

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali called his servant repeatedly; when the servant explained that he trusted Ali's forbearance and felt safe from punishment, Ali approved the answer and freed him.
rows.anchor: وروي عن علي رضي الله عنه أنه صاح بغلام له مرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some explain the question as asking what tricked and enticed the person into neglecting the duty owed to God.
rows.anchor: وناس يقولون: ما غرك: ما خدعك وسول لك، حتى أضعت ما وجب عليك

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud says every person will meet God alone on Judgment Day and be asked what deceived him, what he did with what he knew, and how he answered the messengers.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: ما منكم من أحد إلا وسيخلو الله به يوم القيامة، فيقول له: يا بن آدم ماذا غرك بي؟ يا بن آدم ماذا عملت فيما علمت؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God formed the human from a drop in the womb, giving him two hands, two feet, two eyes, and the rest of his limbs.
rows.anchor: { الذي خلقك } أي قدر خلقك من نطفة { فسواك } في بطن أمك، وجعل لك يدين ورجلين وعينين وسائر أعضائك

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم
rows.claim: The common reading with a doubled dāl means God made the human balanced and well-proportioned; Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim choose it.
rows.anchor: { فعدلك } أي جعلك معتدلا سوي الخلق كما يقال: هذا شيء معدل. وهذه قراءة العامة، وهي اختيار أبي عبيد وأبي حاتم

rows.speaker: الكوفيون: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: The Kufans Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisai read the verb lightly: God inclined and directed the human into whatever form He wished, beautiful or ugly, tall or short.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي: «فعدلك» مخففا أي: أمالك وصرفك إلى أي صورة شاء

words: فِىٓ أَىِّ صُورَةٍۢ مَّا شَآءَ رَكَّبَكَ
rows.speaker: النبي عن موسى بن علي عن أبيه عن جده
rows.claim: Musa ibn Ali reports through his father and grandfather that the Prophet said that, once the sperm settles in the womb, God brings forth every lineage between that person and Adam, in connection with “in whatever image He wished, He composed you.”
rows.anchor: عن جده قال: قال لي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

words: فِىٓ أَىِّ صُورَةٍۢ مَّا شَآءَ رَكَّبَكَ
rows.speaker: عكرمة وأبو صالح
rows.claim: Ikrima and Abu Salih say God may compose a person in a human, donkey, ape, or pig form.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة وأبو صالح: { في أى صورة ما شآء ركبك

words: فِىٓ أَىِّ صُورَةٍۢ مَّا شَآءَ رَكَّبَكَ
rows.speaker: مكحول
rows.claim: Makhul says the form may be male or female, as God wills.
rows.anchor: وقال مكحول: إن شاء ذكرا، وإن شاء أنثى

words: فِىٓ أَىِّ صُورَةٍۢ مَّا شَآءَ رَكَّبَكَ
rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the image is a likeness inherited from a father, mother, paternal uncle, maternal uncle, or another relative.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: «في أي صورة» أي في أي شبه من أب أو أم أو عم أو خال أو غيرهم

words: فِىٓ أَىِّ صُورَةٍۢ مَّا شَآءَ رَكَّبَكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition “fi” attaches to rakkabaka, not ʿadalaka; on the light reading one says ʿadaltu ila, not ʿadaltu fi. Al-Farra therefore rejected that reading when he attached “fi” to ʿadalaka.
rows.anchor: و «في» متعلقة ب «ركبك»، ولا تتعلق ب «عدلك»، على قراءة من خفف لأنك تقول عدلت إلى كذا، ولا تقول عدلت في كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā may be an emphatic extra particle, yielding “in whatever image He wished”; alternatively it is conditional, allowing the image of an animal as well as a human.
rows.anchor: و «ما» يجوز أن تكون صلة مؤكدة أي في أي صورة شاء ركبك. ويجوز أن تكون شرطية أي إن شاء ركبك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation takes kalla to mean “indeed” or “certainly,” introducing an affirmation.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { كلا بل تكذبون بالدين } يجوز أن تكون «كلا» بمعنى حقا و «ألا» فيبتدأ بها

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra takes kalla as “no”: the matter is not as the Meccans claim, whether about their idolatry or the resurrection; it may also mean rebuke and warning against being lulled by God's forbearance.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون بمعنى «لا»، على أن يكون المعنى ليس الأمر كما تقولون من أنكم في عبادتكم غير الله محقون

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says the sound pause is after “the judgment,” or after “He composed you”; pausing after kalla is poor.
rows.anchor: ابن الأنباري: الوقف الجيد على «الدين»، وعلى «ركبك»، والوقف على «كلا» قبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to the people of Mecca, and al-din means the reckoning; bal negates what preceded and confirms the next point. Their denial of resurrection was understood even though this surah had not yet mentioned it.
rows.anchor: { بل تكذبون } يأهل مكة { بالدين } أي بالحساب، و «بل» لنفي شيء تقدم وتحقيق غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He connects the spring to the unseen delights of the Garden promised in al-Sajdah.
rows.anchor: فلا تعلم نفس مآ أخفي لهم من قرة أعين

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Tasnim is a spring flowing through the air by God's power, poured into the vessels of the people of Paradise in measured amounts; when a vessel is full the flow stops, no drop falls to earth, and they need not draw water.
rows.anchor: وقيل: التسنيم عين تجري في الهواء بقدرة الله تعالى، فتنصب في أواني أهل الجنة على قدر مائها

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says they were told that Tasnim flows from beneath the Throne; Hasan's mursal reports say the same.
rows.anchor: ابن زيد: بلغنا أنها عين تجري من تحت العرش. وكذا في مراسيل الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The foremost residents of the Garden of Eden drink Tasnim unmixed, while it is blended for the other people of Paradise.
rows.anchor: أي يشرب منها أهل جنة عدن، وهم أفاضل أهل الجنة، صرفا، وهي لغيرهم مزاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative “ʿaynan” can be a commendatory accusative.
rows.anchor: و «عينا» نصب على المدح

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj treats ʿaynan as a circumstantial accusative from Tasnim, which he regards as a definite name without a known derivation; if derived from sanam, it is an object, like the example from al-Balad.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: نصب على الحال من تسنيم، وتسنيم معرفة، ليس يعرف له اشتقاق

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra also analyzes the accusative as an object governed by Tasnim.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول الفراء إنه منصوب بتسنيم

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash makes ʿaynan depend on yusqawn: they are given to drink a spring, or from a spring.
rows.anchor: وعند الأخفش ب «يسقون» أي يسقون عينا أو من عين

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad supplies an omitted aʿni (“I mean”), making the accusative commendatory.
rows.anchor: وعند المبرد بإضمار أعني على المدح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-insan means humankind generally, addressed as “son of Adam.”
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { يأيها الإنسان إنك كادح إلى ربك كدحا } المراد بالإنسان الجنس أي يابن آدم

rows.speaker: سعيد عن قتادة
rows.claim: Sa'id reports Qatada's exhortation: son of Adam, your striving is weak; if able, make it striving in obedience to God, with no power except by God.
rows.anchor: وكذا روى سعيد عن قتادة: ياابن آدم، إن كدحك لضعيف، فمن استطاع أن يكون كدحه في طاعة الله فليفعل

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil identifies the human as al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Asad.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو معين قال مقاتل: يعني الأسود بن عبد الأسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another identification is Ubayy ibn Khalaf; another takes the address as all unbelievers, addressed as “O unbeliever.”
rows.anchor: ويقال: يعني أبي بن خلف. ويقال: يعني جميع الكفار أيها الكافر إنك كادح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, kadh means work and earning.
rows.anchor: والكدح في كلام العرب: العمل والكسب قال ابن مقبل

rows.speaker: ابن مقبل
rows.claim: Ibn Muqbil's line uses akdahu for striving to earn a living through life's turns.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مقبل: وما الدهر إلا تارتان فمنهما أموت وأخرى أبتغي العيش أكدح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second poetic citation likewise uses akdahu to mean working and striving for life.
rows.anchor: قال آخر: ومضت بشاشة كل عيش صالح وبقيت أكدح للحياة وأنصب أي أعمل

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak reports Ibn Abbas's gloss: you are inevitably returning to your Lord, and kadh means return.
rows.anchor: روى الضحاك عن ابن عباس: «إنك كادح» أي راجع «إلى ربك كدحا» أي رجوعا لا محالة

rows.speaker: القتبي
rows.claim: Al-Qutbi says the person works and labors in his livelihood until meeting his Lord, and meets Him bearing his deeds.
rows.anchor: القتبي «إنك كادح» أي عامل ناصب في معيشتك إلى لقاء ربك. والملاقاة بمعنى اللقاء أي تلقى ربك بعملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the person meets his record of deeds, since the work is over; the following verse's book-taking supports this.
rows.anchor: وقيل أي تلاقي كتاب عملك لأن العمل قد انقضى ولهذا قال: « فأما من أوتي كتابه بيمينه»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person given his book in his right hand is the believer, and his easy reckoning involves no close scrutiny.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { فأما من أوتي كتابه بيمينه } وهو المؤمن { فسوف يحاسب حسابا يسيرا } لا مناقشة فيه

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports the Prophet's explanation that a person who is closely examined in reckoning is punished; the “easy account” is only presentation, not scrutiny. Bukhari, Muslim, and al-Tirmidhi transmit it, and al-Tirmidhi calls it hasan sahih.
rows.anchor: عائشة قالت: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He returns happily to his wives, the houris prepared for him in Paradise, rejoicing with a tranquil heart.
rows.anchor: { وينقلب إلى أهله مسرورا } أزواجه في الجنة من الحور العين «مسرورا» أي مغتبطا قرير العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is also said to have been revealed about Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Asad, the first emigrant from Mecca to Medina; Qatada's interpretation takes his family to be those prepared for him in Paradise.
rows.anchor: ويقال إنها نزلت في أبي سلمة بن عبد الأسد، هو أول من هاجر من مكة إلى المدينة. وقيل: إلى أهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, he returns to the family he had in worldly life to tell them of his deliverance and safety.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إلى أهله الذين كانوا له في الدينا، ليخبرهم بخلاصه وسلامته

words: وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِىَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ وَرَآءَ ظَهْرِهِۦ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse about the book given behind the back was revealed concerning al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Asad, brother of Abu Salamah; it then applies generally to every believer and unbeliever.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { وأما من أوتي كتابه ورآء ظهره } نزلت في الأسود بن عبد الأسد أخي أبي سلمة قاله ابن عباس. ثم هي عامة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the person reaches with his right hand, an angel pulls it away and twists it, and he takes the book with his left hand from behind his back.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يمد يده اليمنى ليأخذ كتابه فيجذبه ملك، فيخلع يمينه، فيأخذ كتابه بشماله من وراء ظهره

rows.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل
rows.claim: Qatada and Muqatil say the chest's plates and bones are opened, the hand enters and emerges from the back, and the person takes the book that way.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة ومقاتل: يفك ألواح صدره وعظامه ثم تدخل يده وتخرج من ظهره، فيأخذ كتابه كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls for destruction, crying “woe to me” and “my destruction.”
rows.anchor: { فسوف يدعو ثبورا } أي بالهلاك فيقول: يا ويلاه، يا ثبوراه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He enters the Fire and suffers its heat.
rows.anchor: { ويصلى سعيرا } أي ويدخل النار حتى يصلى بحرها

rows.speaker: الحرميان وابن عامر والكسائي
rows.claim: The two Meccan readers, Ibn Amir, and al-Kisai read yusallā with a doubled lām as a passive causative; the author compares the form to readings in al-Haqqah and al-Waqi'ah.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحرميان وابن عامر والكسائي «ويصلى» بضم الياء وفتح الصاد، وتشديد اللام كقوله تعالى: ثم الجحيم صلوه

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining readers have the light form with an open yāʾ, an intransitive verb, supported by other descriptions of someone who is to burn in the Fire.
rows.anchor: الباقون «ويصلى» بفتح الياء مخففا، فعل لازم غير متعد

rows.speaker: أبان عن عاصم وخارجة عن نافع وإسماعيل المكي عن ابن كثير
rows.claim: A third reading, reported by Aban from Asim, Kharijah from Nafi, and Ismail al-Makki from Ibn Kathir, has a passive form with a still ṣād and light lām; the source compares it with other readings and the paired forms sallā and aṣlā.
rows.anchor: وقراءة ثالثة رواها أبان عن عاصم وخارجة عن نافع وإسمعيل المكي عن ابن كثير «ويصلى» بضم الياء وإسكان الصاد وفتح اللام مخففا

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says Paradise's people were fearful, sorrowful, tearful, and compassionate in worldly life, then God rewarded them with bliss; people of Hell were cheerful, laughing, and indulging themselves in the world.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد: وصف الله أهل الجنة بالمخافة والحزن والبكاء والشفقة في الدنيا، فأعقبهم به النعيم والسرور في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He thought he would not return alive to be resurrected and called to account, rewarded or punished.
rows.anchor: { إنه ظن أن لن يحور } أي لن يرجع حيا مبعوثا فيحاسب، ثم يثاب أو يعاقب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥāra yaḥūru means to return; Labid's verse describes a bright meteor returning to ash after blazing.
rows.anchor: يقال: حار يحور إذا رجع قال لبيد: وما المرء إلا كالشهاب وضوئه يحور رمادا بعد إذا هو ساطع

rows.speaker: عكرمة وداود بن أبي هند
rows.claim: Ikrima and Dawud ibn Abi Hind say yaḥūru is an Abyssinian word meaning “returns”; the author allows that the two languages may share the same word by derivation.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة وداود بن أبي هند، يحور كلمة بالحبشية، ومعناها يرجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word may also connect with al-khubz al-ḥawārī, bread that returns to whiteness.
rows.anchor: فإنهما كلمة اشتقاق ومنه الخبز الحوارى لأنه يرجع إلى البياض

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says he learned the meaning from an Arab woman calling her daughter ḥūrī, meaning “come back to me”; ḥawr in Arabic means return.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: ما كنت أدري: ما يحور؟ حتى سمعت أعرابية تدعو بنية لها: حورى، أي ارجعي إلي

words: بَلَىٰٓ إِنَّ رَبَّهُۥ كَانَ بِهِۦ بَصِيرًۭا
rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet sought refuge from al-ḥawr after al-kawr, a decline after increase; another transmission has “after al-kawn,” a dispersion after completion.
rows.anchor: اللهم إني أعوذ بك من الحور بعد الكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression “ḥawr in a maḥārah” means one loss after another, used of a person's affairs declining.
rows.anchor: وفي المثل «حور في محارة» أي نقصان في نقصان. يضرب للرجل إذا كان أمره يدبر

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A poet says that blame remains while the group's increase turns into decline, using ḥawr for deterioration.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: واستعجلوا عن خفيف المضغ فازدردوا والذم يبقى وزاد القوم في حور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥāra can mean to return something: a mill that produces no flour “has not returned anything.” Al-hawr can also mean destruction.
rows.anchor: والحور أيضا: الاسم من قولك: طحنت الطاحنة فما أحارت شيئا أي ما ردت شيئا من الدقيق

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd explains the rajaz line's “well with no ḥawr” as a well of destruction, with lā treated as extra.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: أي بئر حور، و «لا» زائدة

rows.speaker: معمر وعبد الرزاق
rows.claim: A variant “after al-kawn” means after affairs have spread out following completion; Ma'mar says the expression is al-kunti, a good person who changes into a bad one.
rows.anchor: وروي «بعد الكون» ومعناه من انتشار الأمر بعد تمامه. وسئل معمر عن الحور بعد الكون، فقال: هو الكنتي

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr says kunti describes an old man who says “I was so in my youth”; a poet's “I became a kunti” illustrates it.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عمرو: يقال للرجل إذا شاخ: كنتي، كأنه نسب إلى قوله: كنت في شبابي كذا. قال: فأصبحت كنتيا

rows.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Ibn al-A'rabi says a kunti boasts “I was young” or “I was brave,” while a kāni says he once had wealth or horses and used to give or ride.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي: الكنتي: هو الذي يقول: كنت شابا، وكنت شجاعا، والكاني هو الذي يقول: كان لي مال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Balā rejects the assumption of no return: the person will indeed return to God.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { بلى } أي ليس الأمر كما ظن، بل يحور إلينا ويرجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God saw him before creating him and knew that his return would be to Him.
rows.anchor: { إن ربه كان به بصيرا } قبل أن يخلقه، عالما بأن مرجعه إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parsing makes “balā” affirm that he will return, then starts a new sentence: his Lord has seen him from creation until resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بلى ليحورن وليرجعن. ثم استأنف فقال: «إن ربه كان به بصيرا» من يوم خلقه إلى أن بعثه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God knows what was decreed for the person, whether wretchedness or felicity.
rows.anchor: وقيل: عالما بما سبق له من الشقاء والسعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The changing stages of life are a clear proof that the world is originated and has a Creator; the philosophers say that changing states show that one's management belongs to another.
rows.anchor: وهذا أدل دليل على حدوث العالم، وإثبات الصانع، قالت الحكماء: من كان اليوم على حالة، وغدا على حالة أخرى

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
rows.claim: Abu Bakr al-Warraq identifies changing conditions, weakness of strength and limbs, and the overcoming or undoing of intentions as proof that the world has a Maker.
rows.anchor: وقيل لأبي بكر الوراق: ما الدليل على أن لهذا العالم صانعا؟ فقال: تحويل الحالات، وعجز القوة، وضعف الأركان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭabaq can mean a group, as in a group of people or locusts arriving.
rows.anchor: ويقال: أتانا طبق من الناس وطبق من الجراد: أي جماعة

rows.speaker: العباس
rows.claim: Al-Abbas's verse about the Prophet moving from loins to womb uses ṭabaq for a generation or people of one era.
rows.anchor: وقول العباس في مدح النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: تنقل من صالب إلى رحم إذا مضى عالم بدا طبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭibāq al-arḍ means filling the earth; ṭabaq also names a thin bone separating the vertebrae and the greater part of the night or day.
rows.anchor: يكون طباق الأرض أي ملأها. والطبق أيضا: عظم رقيق يفصل بين الفقارين. ويقال: مضى طبق من الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is read l-tarkabun with a kasra on the bāʾ, addressing the person, or l-yarkabun with yāʾ, referring to the human.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «لتركبن» بكسر الباء، على خطاب النفس و «ليركبن» بالياء على ليركبن الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “ʿAn ṭabaq” may be an accusative adjective describing one stage as passing beyond another, or a circumstantial phrase attached to the subject pronoun, with form adjusted to the reading.
rows.anchor: و «عن طبق» في محل نصب على أنه صفة ل «طبقا» أي طبقا مجاوزا لطبق. أو حال من الضمير في «لتركبن»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks what prevents them from believing after the signs and proofs have become clear; it is an interrogative of denial.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { فما لهم لا يؤمنون } يعني أي شيء يمنعهم من الإيمان بعد ما وضحت لهم الآيات وقامت الدلالات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is an exclamation: people should marvel at their refusal to believe despite these signs.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تعجب أي اعجبوا منهم في ترك الإيمان مع هذه الآيات

words: وَإِذَا قُرِئَ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْقُرْءَانُ لَا يَسْجُدُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement means that they do not pray.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { وإذا قرىء عليهم القرآن لا يسجدون } أي لا يصلون

words: وَإِذَا قُرِئَ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْقُرْءَانُ لَا يَسْجُدُونَ
rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: In a sound report, Abu Hurayrah recited “When the sky is split open” and prostrated; afterward he told the people that the Prophet had prostrated at this passage.
rows.anchor: وفي الصحيح: إن أبا هريرة قرأ { إذا السمآء انشقت } فسجد فيها، فلما انصرف أخبرهم أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سجد فيها

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik says this is not one of the obligatory prostration passages, because the meaning is that they do not submit or obey its required actions.
rows.anchor: وقد قال مالك: إنها ليست من عزائم السجود لأن المعنى لا يذعنون ولا يطيعون في العمل بواجباته

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says it is an obligatory prostration passage, as in the Medinese report from Malik, supported by Qur'an and Sunna.
rows.anchor: ابن العربي: والصحيح أنها منه، وهي رواية المدنيين عنه، وقد اعتضد فيها القرآن والسنة

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says he avoided reciting the passage when leading people: prostrating would be rejected, while omitting it would be a shortcoming, so he recited it only when praying alone.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي: لما أممت بالناس تركت قراءتها لأني إن سجدت أنكروه، وإن تركتها كان تقصيرا مني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage directs people to consider their first origin so they know the one who created them can restore and recompense them; they should prepare for resurrection and give their recorders only deeds that benefit them.
rows.anchor: وجه الاتصال بما قبله توصية الإنسان بالنظر في أول أمره وسنته الأولى، حتى يعلم أن من أنشأه قادر على إعادته وجزائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-insan here means the son of Adam.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { فلينظر الإنسان } أي ابن آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Mimma khuliqa” is an interrogative: from what was he created? “Khuliqa” supplies the answer.
rows.anchor: و { مم خلق }؟ استفهام أي من أي شيء خلق؟ ثم قال: { خلق } وهو جواب الاستفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dāfiq water is semen; dafq means pouring water out, and the word dāfiq describes water poured out.
rows.anchor: { من مآء دافق } أي من المني. والدفق: صب الماء، دفقت الماء أدفقه دفقا: صببته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dāfiq is an active-form word with passive sense, like sirr kātim for a secret that is concealed; the expression is based on dufiq al-māʾ, and one does not say dafaqa al-māʾ. Daafa Allah rūḥahu is a curse wishing death.
rows.anchor: فهو ماء دافق، أي مدفوق كما قالوا: سر كاتم: أي مكتوم لأنه من قولك: دفق الماء، على ما لم يسم فاعله

rows.speaker: الفراء والأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Farra and al-Akhfash gloss dāfiq as water poured into the womb.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء والأخفش: «من ماء دافق» أي مصبوب في الرحم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj takes dāfiq as “water possessing an outpouring.”
rows.anchor: الزجاج: من ماء ذي اندفاق. يقال: دارع وفارس ونابل أي ذو فرس، ودرع، ونبل

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh's analysis makes dāfiq the water flowing with great force.
rows.anchor: وهذا مذهب سيبويه. فالدافق هو المندفق بشدة قوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two fluids, the man's and the woman's, are intended, but are called one water because they mix.
rows.anchor: وأراد ماءين: ماء الرجل وماء المرأة لأن الإنسان مخلوق منهما، لكن جعلهما ماء واحدا لامتزاجهما

rows.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ikrima reports from Ibn Abbas that dāfiq means viscous.
rows.anchor: وعن عكرمة عن ابن عباس: «دافق» لزج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water comes from between the ṣulb, meaning the back; the word has four forms: ṣulb, ṣulub, ṣulb with fatḥa on the lām, and ṣālib, on the pattern qālib.
rows.anchor: { يخرج } أي هذا الماء { من بين الصلب } أي الظهر. وفيه لغات أربع: صلب، وصلب وقرىء بهما وصلب بفتح اللام، وصالب على وزن قالب

rows.speaker: العباس
rows.claim: Al-Abbas's verse about transmission from a loin to a womb attests the form ṣālib.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول العباس: تنقل من صالب إلى رحم

rows.speaker: العباس
rows.claim: Al-Abbas's line also attests ṣālib as a word for the loin in the phrase about moving from loin to womb.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول العباس: تنقل من صالب إلى رحم

rows.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك
rows.claim: Mujahid and al-Dahhak say God can return the fluid to the urethra.
rows.anchor: { إنه } أي إن الله جل ثناؤه { على رجعه } أي على رد الماء في الإحليل، { لقادر } كذا قال مجاهد والضحاك

rows.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك وعكرمة
rows.claim: A second view from Mujahid and al-Dahhak, also attributed to Ikrima, is that God can return the fluid to the backbone.
rows.anchor: وعنهما أيضا أن المعنى: إنه على رد الماء في الصلب وقاله عكرمة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak also says God can return the human to fluid, as he was before.
rows.anchor: وعن الضحاك أيضا أن المعنى: إنه على رد الإنسان ماء كما كان لقادر

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak also interprets the return as God's ability to move a person from old age back to youth and from youth to old age; al-Mahdawi gives the same account.
rows.anchor: وعنه أيضا أن المعنى: إنه على رد الإنسان من الكبر إلى الشباب، ومن الشباب إلى الكبر، لقادر. وكذا في المهدوي

rows.speaker: الماوردي والثعلبي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi and al-Tha'labi give another sequence: return from old age to childhood, and from childhood to the sperm stage.
rows.anchor: وفي الماوردي والثعلبي: إلى الصبا، ومن الصبا إلى النطفة

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says God can withhold the fluid so that it does not emerge.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: إنه على حبس ذلك الماء حتى لا يخرج، لقادر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة والحسن وعكرمة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, al-Hasan, and Ikrima say God can return the person after death; al-Tabari chooses this view, and al-Tha'labi calls it strongest because of the following verse about secrets being exposed.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وقتادة والحسن وعكرمة أيضا: إنه على رد الإنسان بعد الموت لقادر

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi allows that God will return the person to worldly life after resurrection, as unbelievers ask God for a return.
rows.anchor: قال الماوردي: ويحتمل أنه على أن يعيده إلى الدنيا بعد بعثه في الآخرة لأن الكفار يسألون الله تعالى فيها الرجعة
